title: Forces and elasticity
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Physics (8463) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.5.3-c02, 4.5.3-c03, 4.5.3-c01, 4.5.3-c08. Clues: 4.5.3-c02 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c03 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c01 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c08 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.5.3-q01, 4.5.3-q02, 4.5.3-q03, 4.5.3-q04, 4.5.3-q05, 4.5.3-q06, 4.5.3-q07, 4.5.3-q08, 4.5.3-q09, 4.5.3-q10, 4.5.3-q11, 4.5.3-q12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Stretching
items.clue: Making an object longer by pulling its ends apart.

items.label: Compressing
items.clue: Making an object shorter by pushing its ends towards each other.

items.label: Deformation
items.clue: A change in the shape of an object caused by forces acting on it.

items.label: Extension
items.clue: The increase in length of an object compared with its original, unloaded length.

questions.stem: A rubber band is held by a clamp at one end while a student pulls the other end, and the band stretches. Which statement describes the forces that stretch the band?

options.text: Two forces act on the band, pulling its two ends in opposite directions.
One pulling force acts on the band, along the line of the band.
Two forces act on the band, both pulling it towards the clamp.
The weight of the band is the only force acting, and it stretches it.

questions.explanation: Deforming a stationary object needs more than one force, and to stretch it the forces must pull the ends apart.

questions.stem: A car is parked on level ground and the springs in its suspension are squashed. Which pair of forces compresses one of these springs?

options.text: The weight of the car is the only force acting on the spring.
The car body pushes down on the spring and the axle pushes up on it.
The car body and the axle both push down on the spring from above it.
The spring squashes under its own weight as it hangs there.

questions.explanation: Compression needs two forces pushing the ends of the spring towards each other.

questions.stem: Why must more than one force be applied to a stationary object in order to change its shape?

options.text: A single force on its own is enough to stretch the object into a new shape.
Forces always occur in pairs, so a second force appears without being applied.
A single force would leave a resultant force, so the object would accelerate.
One force by itself will stretch the object, so no second force is needed.

questions.explanation: With one force there is a resultant force; the object would move off rather than deform, so a second force is needed.

options.text: The object keeps part of its extra length after the forces are removed.
The object is made of rubber, so it stretches much further than metal does.
The object breaks into pieces as soon as the stretching force is removed.
The object returns to its original shape once the forces are removed.

questions.explanation: Elastic deformation is defined by full recovery of the original shape when the forces are removed.

questions.stem: A steel spring is stretched by a very large force. When the force is removed the spring is longer than it was at the start. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It has been elastically deformed, because its shape changed while pulled.
It has been inelastically deformed, so it has not returned to its original shape.
It cannot have deformed elastically, since steel is not a stretchy material.
It has been inelastically deformed, so the metal has begun to break apart.

questions.explanation: Not returning to the original length after the force is removed is exactly inelastic deformation.

questions.stem: A spring is loaded with weights, staying below its limit of proportionality. Which statement about the force and the extension is correct?

options.text: The extension is directly proportional to the total length of the spring used.
The force is proportional to the extension whatever the load size.
The extension is directly proportional to the force applied to the spring.
The extension is proportional to the spring constant of that spring.

questions.explanation: This is the specification statement: extension is directly proportional to force below the limit of proportionality.

questions.stem: What does the limit of proportionality of a spring tell you?

options.text: The force at which the spring finally snaps and can carry no more load.
The force beyond which the spring will not return to its original length.
The largest length the spring reaches before it stops stretching.
The largest force for which extension stays proportional to force.

questions.explanation: Up to this force the graph is a straight line through the origin; beyond it, proportionality is lost.

questions.stem: A spring has a spring constant of 120 N/m and is stretched by 25 cm, which is below its limit of proportionality. Using force = spring constant × extension, what is the force applied to the spring?
Which statement about the quantities in the equation F = k e is correct?

options.text: The spring constant, k, is measured in newtons, N, as a force is.
The extension, e, is measured in centimetres, cm, in this equation.
The spring constant, k, is measured in newtons per metre, written N/m.
The extension, e, is the whole length of the stretched spring.

questions.explanation: F is in newtons, k is in newtons per metre and e is in metres.

questions.stem: A force of 6.0 N stretches a spring by 12 cm. The limit of proportionality has not been exceeded. What is the spring constant of this spring?

options.text: 50 N/m

questions.stem: Spring A has a spring constant of 30 N/m and spring B has a spring constant of 90 N/m. The same force is applied to each spring. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Spring B extends less, because a larger spring constant means a stiffer spring.
Spring B extends more, because a larger spring constant means more stretch.
Both springs extend by exactly the same amount, because the same force is applied.
Spring B extends three times as far as spring A does under this force.

questions.explanation: Since e = F / k, a larger spring constant gives a smaller extension for the same force.

questions.stem: A spring is squashed rather than stretched. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A different equation is needed, because F = k e only covers stretching.
F = k e still applies, with e as the compression of the spring.
No energy is stored, because energy is only stored by stretching a spring.
The spring constant becomes negative when the spring is compressed.

questions.explanation: The specification states that the relationship also applies to compression, with e as the compression.
